projects.title: Short-Horizon Crypto Volatility & Direction Research
projects.summary: Forecasting price ranges and direction on 1-second market data, with leakage checks, placebo tests and fee-aware walk-forward backtests.
projects.problem: Can short-horizon price ranges and direction be predicted well enough to matter after trading costs? Most retail backtests skip leakage and fee checks, so the goal was to answer this honestly.
built: Volatility model: ridge regression on multi-window realised variance, activity, jumps and time-of-day features.
Price ranges from volatility-scaled return quantiles, recalibrated on a rolling window.
Direction model: heavily regularised logistic regression on order-flow imbalance, recent returns and futures–spot basis, only enabled when it beats the base rate out of sample.
A small wide-and-deep neural net written in plain NumPy that learns a residual correction, with early stopping.
Local paper-trading dashboards and auto-generated markdown reports. No real orders.
ml: Horizon study from 10 seconds to 20 minutes.
Placebo test with shuffled labels and a synthetic no-signal test to catch leakage.
outcome: Range forecasts came out well calibrated.
Direction signal was weak, close to chance.
No strategy was profitable after fees, and the reports say so plainly.
projects.note: Personal research project. The value is in the evaluation discipline: a negative result reported honestly.

projects.title: Retail Purchase-Order Demand Forecasting
projects.summary: Gradient-boosting ensemble that predicts monthly purchase-order quantities per article for retail chain customers, built to support stock planning.
projects.problem: Stock for chain-store customers was planned from simple averages, which reacts slowly to trends and seasonality.
built: Feature set of 60+ lag and rolling-window statistics (mean, std, min, max) plus encoded category.
Ensemble of XGBoost, LightGBM and gradient boosting, with random forest as a comparison.
Evaluated with 5-fold CV on MAE, then MAE, RMSE, R² and MAPE on a held-out month.
ml: Hold-out evaluation on the most recent month.
outcome: Runs offline as a notebook and script. It is not yet wired into the planning app.
Sits next to a rules-based planner (weighted averages, trend and ABC classification) that is in daily use.

projects.title: Modern Trade Sales & Stock Planning Platform
projects.summary: Flask platform that consolidates retail-chain sales and purchase orders, and plans stock with ABC classification, trend detection and stock-cover rules.
projects.problem: Sales, purchase-order and stock data for chain-store customers arrived as separate files in different formats, so planning and reporting were manual.
built: ETL jobs that load distributor and customer files into consolidated MySQL tables.
Dashboards by article, store, category and state, plus sales vs. target, exported as heat-mapped Excel.
Purchase-order mapper and master-data management.
Demand planner using weighted-average sales, trend classification, ABC classes, stock cover and pipeline, with editable multipliers.
Generates order files with product thumbnails. Login, registration and email password reset.
outcome: One place for the team to see sales against target and plan replenishment instead of merging files by hand.

projects.title: Sales & Inventory Reporting System (ETL + Portal)
projects.summary: ETL pipelines that turn ERP extracts into report tables, served through a role-based Flask portal where each user sees only their regions.
projects.problem: Daily stock and sales reports were assembled by hand from ERP extracts and spreadsheets, then sent around as files.
built: ETL scripts for new launches, depot stock, leftover stock, category mix, sales-plan accuracy and dealer-wise sales.
Flask portal with filterable admin and user dashboards, and Excel export with embedded product images.
Region-based access control, roles, session timeouts and logging.
Admin uploads for finance-related files that feed the reports.
Experiment: a chat endpoint that asks a hosted open-weights LLM to answer questions over KPI summaries.
outcome: Reports are generated by scheduled scripts instead of by hand, and users pull their own region's view.

projects.title: Product Image Search Bot with Nightly Sync ETL
projects.summary: Chat-style product image search with OTP login and admin analytics, kept current by a nightly ETL that syncs only changed images from cloud storage.
projects.problem: Sales teams needed current product images quickly, but the image library was large, changed often and was hard to search.
built: Search by article, colour or category with type-ahead, or upload a stock list. Results come back as images, Excel or ZIP.
Scheduled ETL that compares content hashes to download only new or replaced images, and writes exception reports.
Rule-based name parsing (regex + colour mapping) to standardise image names into a master file.
Security: OTP email login, admin-approved registration, HMAC single-sign-on tokens from sibling apps, encrypted secrets, password hashing.
Admin analytics: searches, trending items, not-found items and daily usage.
outcome: Incremental sync avoids re-downloading the full library every night.
Not-found search analytics show which images are missing.

projects.title: Stock-to-Image Catalogue Generator
projects.summary: Upload a stock list and get back an illustrated PDF catalogue, an Excel file with images or a ZIP, joined with product master and MRP data.
projects.problem: Building a picture catalogue for a stock list meant looking up each article's image and price by hand.
built: Joins uploaded stock with a cached product master and MRP data.
Finds images, stamps them with the article code, and builds PDF catalogues (ReportLab) and Excel files with embedded images.
Parallel, resumable image downloader from cloud object storage with retries.
Missing-image tracking with a scheduled email report, user management and activity logging.
outcome: A catalogue that took manual lookups is produced from one upload.

projects.title: Product Launch Mailer
projects.summary: Turns a launch spreadsheet into region-wise HTML emails with product images and attachments, and flags articles that are missing images.
projects.problem: Launch announcements were assembled and sent region by region by hand, and missing images were often found only after sending.
built: Reads the launch file and joins it with a colour map and product images.
Lists articles with missing images for download before anything is sent.
Region-to-recipient mapping stored in SQLite.
HTML emails with inlined CSS, embedded images and attachments, sent over SMTP, with a launch history log.
Single-sign-on hand-off to the image search bot.
outcome: A repeatable launch mail process with a check for missing images before sending.

projects.title: Power BI Embedded Sales Portal
projects.summary: Flask portal that embeds Power BI reports with per-user access, admin-managed report pages and filters, and DAX-driven Excel export.
projects.problem: Different users needed different slices of the same Power BI reports without each one needing a Power BI licence or workspace access.
built: Server-side Azure AD authentication and Power BI REST calls to generate embed settings.
Admin screens to register reports, pages and filters and to grant access per user.
DAX queries to discover columns and values for filter menus, and to export data to Excel.
User and activity tracking with auto-logout.
outcome: Users see only the reports they are allowed to, inside one portal.

projects.title: Production Planning Software (PPS)
projects.summary: Flask application that converts daily dealer requirements into machine and mould schedules using historical sales and mould–machine compatibility.
projects.problem: Daily production plans were built by hand from dealer requirements, mould availability and machine capacity.
built: Pulls daily requirements and runs a rules-based scheduler over mould–machine compatibility and capacity.
Machine-wise schedule view with priorities, a backlog view of unallocated requirements, and Excel export.
Admin screens for the mould compatibility matrix and machine capacity.
outcome: Planners generate the day's schedule from the app instead of building it in spreadsheets.
projects.note: Runs on a company server. Described at a high level only.

projects.title: Dealer Stock Allotment Engine
projects.summary: Script that allocates limited stock against daily dealer requirements using weighted priority, inventory class and recent sales trend.
projects.problem: When demand exceeds stock, deciding which dealer gets what was manual and inconsistent.
built: Multi-factor scoring that combines priority, inventory class and recent trend.
Three-tier classification (green / red / black) to decide full, partial or no allotment.
Produces an allotment file for the distribution team.
outcome: The same rules are applied every day instead of case-by-case decisions.
projects.note: Runs on a company server. Described at a high level only.
